questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. The ulcer has clean-cut edges and a firm, indurated base. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. Which of the following statements is MOST accurate?
opts: The causative organism is Haemophilus ducreyi
VDRL becomes reactive within 24 hours of appearance of the chancre
The regional lymph nodes are typically tender and suppurate
The chancre heals spontaneously even without treatment
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents with a painless, indurated chancre caused by Treponema pallidum. The chancre heals spontaneously in 3-6 weeks regardless of treatment. VDRL becomes reactive 1-4 weeks after chancre appearance. Tender, suppurating nodes suggest chancroid (H. ducreyi).

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman with HIV (CD4 count 50/µL) develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the left T6 dermatome. After 3 days, vesicles become pustular and hemorrhagic. The MOST appropriate antiviral regimen is:
opts: Valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily for 3 days
Famciclovir 125 mg twice daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster in an immunocompromised patient (HIV with CD4 <200) requires higher-dose oral acyclovir: 800 mg 5 times/day for 7-10 days or IV acyclovir if severe/disseminated. Standard doses used in immunocompetent patients are insufficient for immunocompromised hosts.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT for 6 months develops sudden erythema and swelling of existing skin lesions, with fever and pain in peripheral nerves. Nerve conduction studies show acute deterioration. This reaction is BEST classified as:
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL) due to sudden increase in cell-mediated immunity. It manifests as upgrading of existing lesions with acute neuritis. ENL (Type 2) occurs in BL/LL with new tender nodules. Lucio phenomenon is a rare necrotizing reaction in diffuse lepromatous leprosy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a 2-year history of butterfly-shaped erythema on the face, photosensitivity, and painful oral ulcers. ANA is positive (1:640, homogeneous pattern). Anti-dsDNA is elevated. Which renal manifestation is MOST specific for her diagnosis?
questions.exp: In SLE nephritis, Class IV (diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis) is the most common and most severe form, occurring in ~40-50% of lupus nephritis cases. It carries the worst prognosis and is most strongly associated with active systemic disease and elevated anti-dsDNA.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing skin and urticarial plaques. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. The autoantibodies target:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is characterized by tense bullae, linear IgG/C3 at DEJ on DIF, and autoantibodies against BP180 (BPAG2/Col XVII) and BP230 (BPAG1). Desmoglein 1 and 3 are targets in pemphigus foliaceus and vulgaris respectively. Type VII collagen is targeted in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with verrucous plaques on the cheeks, forehead, and scalp with follicular plugging, central scarring, and peripheral hyperpigmentation. Histology shows hyperkeratosis, follicular plugging, vacuolar degeneration of basal layer, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE) presents with scarring plaques with follicular plugging, central atrophy, and peripheral hyperpigmentation on sun-exposed areas. Histology shows hyperkeratosis, follicular plugging, vacuolar change at DEJ, and perivascular infiltrate. DLE rarely progresses to SLE (<5%).

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with multiple pearly, skin-colored, umbilicated papules on the face, trunk, and genitalia. CD4 count is 150/µL. The MOST appropriate initial treatment is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum in HIV patients with CD4 <200/µL tends to be extensive and disfiguring. The cornerstone of treatment is optimization of ART to restore immune function (increase CD4 count), which leads to resolution of molluscum. Local destructive therapies may be used as adjuncts but do not address the underlying immunodeficiency.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man who works outdoors presents with a slowly growing, pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias on his nose. The center ulcerates. Which statement about this condition is CORRECT?
opts: It most commonly metastasizes to regional lymph nodes
It arises from the stratum granulosum
Morpheaform (sclerosing) subtype has the highest recurrence rate
Mohs micrographic surgery has a 5-year cure rate of 50-60%
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) arises from basal keratinocytes/follicular stem cells. Morpheaform BCC has ill-defined borders with subclinical spread, leading to higher recurrence rates after conventional excision. BCC rarely metastasizes (<0.5%). Mohs surgery achieves 5-year cure rates of >98% for primary BCC.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with recurrent, well-defined, erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the elbows, knees, and scalp for 5 years. She now has pitting, onycholysis, and subungual hyperkeratosis. The MOST specific nail finding for psoriasis is:
questions.exp: Oil drop sign (salmon patch — onycholysis with yellowish-brown discoloration under the nail plate) is the most specific nail finding for psoriasis. Pitting is the most common nail finding in psoriasis but can occur in alopecia areata and eczema too. Beau's lines and leukonychia are non-specific.

questions.q: A 40-year-old farmer from rural India develops a painless nodule on his foot that slowly enlarges over months. The nodule drains thick pus with black granules. X-ray shows bony destruction. The MOST likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Mycetoma with black granules is most commonly caused by Madurella mycetomatis (eumycetoma). White/yellow granules suggest actinomycetoma (Nocardia, Actinomadura). Black granules specifically point to fungal (eumycetoma) causes. Treatment differs: actinomycetoma responds to antibiotics, eumycetoma requires antifungals ± surgery.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with painful genital ulcers with a soft, ragged, undermined edge and painful, tender inguinal lymphadenopathy that becomes fluctuant. Gram stain of pus shows 'school of fish' pattern. Treatment of choice is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 21 days
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) presents with painful, soft ulcer with undermined edges and tender inguinal buboes. Gram stain shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' pattern. Treatment options include azithromycin 1g single dose, ceftriaxone 250mg IM, or ciprofloxacin 500mg BD×3 days. Single-dose azithromycin ensures compliance.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, skin tightening of the fingers and face, telangiectasias, and calcinosis. CREST syndrome is diagnosed. Which antibody is MOST specific for this presentation?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) represents limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc). Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is highly specific for lcSSc/CREST (~70-80%). Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc with pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-Jo-1 is seen in polymyositis/dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with hypopigmented patches with loss of sensation. BI of 0 at all sites. Skin biopsy shows granulomas around dermal nerves with epithelioid cells, Langerhans giant cells, but NO acid-fast bacilli. Classification and treatment:
questions.exp: BI of 0 at all sites with well-formed epithelioid granulomas and no AFB is consistent with tuberculoid (TT) leprosy — classified as paucibacillary under WHO MDT criteria (BI=0). PB-MDT (rifampicin monthly + dapsone daily) for 6 months is the treatment. MB-MDT (12 months) is used when BI>0 at any site.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl with Grade III-IV acne has not responded to topical retinoids and topical antibiotics. The MOST appropriate next treatment is:
questions.exp: For moderate-to-severe inflammatory acne (Grade III-IV) not responding to topical therapy, oral antibiotics (tetracyclines — doxycycline or tetracycline) combined with topical retinoids are the next step. Oral isotretinoin is reserved for severe nodulo-cystic acne (Grade IV-V), treatment-resistant cases, or acne with scarring.

questions.q: A wood-cutter develops a painless papule on his hand that ulcerates and is followed by a chain of nodules ascending along the lymphatics of the forearm. KOH preparation of the ulcer is negative. The diagnosis and drug of choice are:
questions.exp: Sporotrichoid spread (ascending lymphangitis with nodules) after trauma from plant/wood injury is classic for Sporothrix schenckii (sporotrichosis). Itraconazole 100-200 mg/day for 3-6 months is the drug of choice. Saturated potassium iodide (SSKI) is an alternative. KOH is usually negative as the fungal load is low in tissue.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman develops tense bullae on the abdomen during the 3rd trimester of pregnancy. The lesions are extremely pruritic and begin periumbilically. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear C3 and IgG at the DEJ. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Pemphigoid gestationis is a rare autoimmune bullous disorder of pregnancy. It begins periumbilically, presents with tense bullae in late pregnancy, and shows linear C3 (most reliable) and IgG at DEJ on DIF. Autoantibodies are against BP180. PUPPP presents in striae without bullae. Cholestasis presents with pruritus without primary skin lesions.

questions.q: A 68-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing ulcerated lesion on the lower lip over 6 weeks. He is a chronic smoker and farmer. Biopsy shows nests of atypical squamous cells invading the dermis with keratin pearls. Regional cervical lymph nodes are enlarged. The 5-year survival with nodal involvement is approximately:
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the lip carries a relatively poor prognosis when regional lymph nodes are involved. With nodal metastasis, 5-year survival drops to approximately 40-50%. Without nodal involvement, 5-year survival is ~80-90%. Risk factors include UV exposure, tobacco, immunosuppression, and chronic wounds.

questions.q: A patient treated with dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia. G6PD deficiency is confirmed. What is the BEST immediate management?
opts: Continue dapsone at a reduced dose
questions.exp: Methemoglobinemia (MetHb >30% causing symptoms) is treated with IV methylene blue 1-2 mg/kg, which acts as an electron carrier to reduce MetHb to Hb. In G6PD deficiency, methylene blue's efficacy is reduced (requires NADPH generated by G6PD). Still, it is the initial treatment for significant methemoglobinemia, and dapsone should be stopped.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents to the STD clinic with multiple, painless, flesh-colored papules with a cauliflower-like surface on the perianal region. The MOST common causative HPV types are:
questions.exp: Condyloma acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused predominantly by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11, which account for ~90% of cases. HPV 16 and 18 (high-risk) are associated with anogenital carcinomas. HPV 1 and 2 cause common warts (verruca vulgaris). HPV 31, 33 are intermediate-risk types.

questions.q: A biopsy from a hypopigmented patch in a leprosy patient shows a superficial and deep perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate with rare poorly-formed granulomas. No AFB are seen. Nerves are mildly affected. The histological classification is:
questions.exp: BT (borderline tuberculoid) leprosy shows less well-formed granulomas than TT, with epithelioid cells but fewer giant cells, more lymphocytes, and slight nerve involvement. The granulomas do not reach the epidermis (unlike TT). BB shows poorly organized granulomas. Indeterminate shows only a mild perivascular infiltrate without granulomas.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with painful erosions in the mouth and flaccid bullae on the trunk. Nikolsky sign is positive. Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin shows intercellular IgG deposits in a 'chicken-wire' pattern. The TARGET antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) targets desmoglein 3 (Dsg3, 130 kDa), predominantly expressed in mucous membranes. When both Dsg3 and Dsg1 are targeted, skin lesions also appear. Mucosal-dominant PV targets Dsg3 alone. BP180 is targeted in bullous pemphigoid. Envoplakin/periplakin are targeted in paraneoplastic pemphigus.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman develops severe stomatitis, blistering of the lips, conjunctivitis, and target lesions with epidermal detachment involving >30% of body surface area, 2 weeks after starting phenytoin. The MOST appropriate management is:
opts: Immediate withdrawal of phenytoin and supportive care in a burns unit
questions.exp: Stevens-Johnson syndrome/Toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN) requires immediate withdrawal of the causative drug and supportive care in a burns unit or ICU. This is the universally agreed upon management. The role of corticosteroids is controversial and generally not recommended. IVIG and cyclosporine are used as adjuncts in some centers. Causative drug withdrawal is the single most critical step.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with painful scrotal swelling and urethral discharge. Gram stain of urethral smear shows intracellular Gram-negative diplococci. If untreated, the MOST feared complication leading to infertility is:
questions.exp: Gonococcal urethritis (Neisseria gonorrhoeae) complicated by epididymo-orchitis can lead to infertility if bilateral or if scarring occurs from delayed treatment. Reiter's syndrome (reactive arthritis) is a complication of non-gonococcal urethritis (Chlamydia). Fournier's gangrene is a necrotizing fasciitis, not a direct complication of gonorrhea.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man on cyclosporine for 6 months develops redness, scaling, perifollicular erythema, and areas of scarring alopecia on the scalp with polytrichia (tufting of hairs). This presentation is MOST consistent with:
questions.exp: Folliculitis decalvans is a neutrophilic scarring alopecia characterized by perifollicular pustules and erythema leading to progressive scarring with polytrichia (tufted hairs). It is associated with Staphylococcus aureus colonization and is more common in immunosuppressed patients. Kerion is a boggy, tender mass from fungal infection. Pityriasis amiantacea shows thick asbestos-like scales adherent to hair shafts without scarring.

questions.q: PUVA phototherapy is planned for a severe psoriasis patient. Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE contraindication?
opts: History of non-melanoma skin cancer treated 10 years ago
questions.exp: Pregnancy is an absolute contraindication to PUVA (psoralen + UVA) because psoralens are mutagenic and potentially teratogenic. Other absolute contraindications include lupus erythematosus, porphyria, and xeroderma pigmentosum. History of previous SCC/BCC and mild renal impairment are relative contraindications.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with diffuse hair loss 3 months after delivering a healthy baby. The hair loss is diffuse and non-scarring. Pull test shows >6 hairs from a single tug. The MOST likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Postpartum hair loss occurring 2-4 months after delivery is classic telogen effluvium. During pregnancy, high estrogen prolongs anagen phase. After delivery, estrogen drops and many follicles shift to telogen simultaneously, causing diffuse, non-scarring shedding. It is self-limiting with regrowth within 6-12 months.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man with 20-year psoriasis develops asymmetric oligoarthritis affecting DIP joints and 'sausage digits' (dactylitis). X-ray shows 'pencil-in-cup' deformity. Which of the following statements is correct?
opts: This pattern is called arthritis mutilans and is the most severe form
HLA-B27 is positive in >90% of cases
Sacroiliac joint involvement is never seen
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis with 'pencil-in-cup' deformity on X-ray represents arthritis mutilans — the most severe and destructive form characterized by osteolysis. Psoriatic arthritis is seronegative (RF negative). HLA-B27 is positive in ~20-30% of cases. Sacroiliitis and spondylitis can occur in psoriatic arthritis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old construction worker presents with marked hyperpigmentation on sun-exposed areas, areas of leucoderma, and atrophy at the same sites. He admits to using a skin-lightening cream containing hydroquinone. The clinical picture is consistent with:
questions.exp: Long-term use of skin-lightening creams containing hydroquinone can cause paradoxical hyperpigmentation (exogenous ochronosis — bluish-black pigmentation due to ochre deposits in dermis) along with depigmentation and atrophy. This triad (hyperpigmentation + leucoderma + atrophy) from bleaching cream use points to exogenous ochronosis.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the mouth and nose. Culture grows beta-hemolytic Streptococcus. The MOST dangerous systemic complication is:
questions.exp: Impetigo caused by Group A Streptococcus (GAS) can be complicated by post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN), caused by nephritogenic strains (e.g., M type 49). This is the most dangerous systemic complication of streptococcal impetigo. Notably, rheumatic fever follows pharyngitis, NOT impetigo. Staphylococcal impetigo does not cause PSGN.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and hypopyon uveitis. She also has a positive pathergy test. The MOST common cause of death in this condition is:
questions.exp: Behcet's disease (oral ulcers + genital ulcers + uveitis + positive pathergy test) is a systemic vasculitis. The most feared vascular complication and leading cause of death is pulmonary artery aneurysm with massive hemoptysis, which can be life-threatening. CNS involvement is common but cerebral venous thrombosis is less lethal than pulmonary hemorrhage.
